rationale: Lycopolitan body-anatomy term for the principal divisions of the body (distinct from Greek-loan ⲙⲉⲗⲟⲥ 'member'). In this kephalaion, the great-limbs / small-wellsprings / members triadic schema parallels the cosmological storehouses / elements / dark-substances triad. Likely related to Coptic ⲁⲧⲉ/ⲏⲧⲉ 'joint, limb' (Crum 17b, 642a) with Lycopolitan doubled ⲧⲧ.

Compound of Coptic verbal ⲣ̄- ('become, do') + Greek loan ἀργός ('idle, inactive'). The Manichaean technical antithesis to ⲉⲛⲉⲣⲅⲓⲁ ('operation'): the storehouses without their natures become 'argon' (operationless), exactly as the body without its soul ceases to have energeia (lines 25-26). Preserves the Greek philosophical-physical register.

Greek loanword ἄκρον 'tip, extreme point.' In line 4 the members emerge ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ⲙ̄ⲡⲁⲕⲣⲟⲛ 'from the extremity' of the small wellsprings — the technical anatomical-cosmological term for the outermost terminal of a structure where productive emergence occurs.

Apparent expanded variant of ⲡϣⲓⲭϩ 'abyss, pit' (in accumulated vocabulary). Designates the cosmological locus in which Hyle and her powers existed in their storehouses prior to the cosmogonic separation. The intercalated ⲗ may be scribal or reflect a dialectal compound form.

Lycopolitan variant of ⲙⲟⲩϫⲧ̄/ⲙⲟⲩⲝⲧ̄ 'mingle' (in accumulated vocabulary as ⲙⲟⲩⲝⲧ̄). The ⲁ-vowel form may be qualitative or a dialectal variation. Used here of the great limbs being inwardly intermingled with the body — preparing the cosmological analogy of elements mingled in Hyle's storehouses.
